correctness.rationale: The local-chord bound is deterministic: a chord with j endpoints in its shorter arc crosses at most j partners. Fixing K disjoint chords leaves a uniform (n-K)-chord diagram after order-preserving deletion; the loss of crossings is between zero and KJ. Exact cycle-matchings enumeration proves the factorial mark count, yielding the finite transform. The published crossing CLT with O(n^{-1/2}) Kolmogorov rate, classical mean and variance, and the deletion sandwich imply uniformly conditional normality. Compatible length-mark arrays have (2n)^K(1+O(1/n)) possibilities and each occurs with matching inclusion probability, giving mixed factorial convergence; Poisson moment determinacy and uniform integrability establish full independent product convergence. Exact enumeration n=2..7 checks the finite transform and the loss bound, but is not used as an asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: Joint convergence gives a rigorous independent Gaussian global crossing signal alongside arbitrary fixed vectors of order-one Poisson local defects; separate marginal limit theorems are insufficient for simultaneous inference. The location-uniform conditional normal approximation and an exact finite factorial deletion transform identify the mechanism and apply beyond second moments. The fixed-length condition and the robust all-placement bound make the result a natural structural theorem about locality versus global combinatorial fluctuations, not an arbitrary finite count.
